papers.title_en: Progressive multi-scale tumor-state memory for incomplete multimodal brain tumor segmentation
papers.authors: Milad Rostamian, Mohammadreza Mohammadi, Mohsen Soryani
papers.evidence: 应对模态缺失的多模态MRI融合分割
papers.tldr: 脑肿瘤分割依赖多种MRI序列，但部分序列常缺失并改变各肿瘤区域可用证据。作者提出PMTM，在编码器各阶段维护紧凑肿瘤状态，用分配图池化可用模态证据并经门控更新状态，以引导残差融合和模态交互。在BraTS2018、2020和2023 GLI全部15种非空模态子集上，三区域平均Dice分别为75.31%、77.54%、80.47%，均高于RobustSeg、RFNet和mmFormer。该框架跨阶段保留和更新肿瘤证据，支持不完整多模态脑肿瘤分割。
papers.abstract_en: Brain tumor segmentation uses complementary magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) sequences, but some sequences may be unavailable in practice. Their absence changes the information available for segmenting different tumor regions. Fusion methods can support different input subsets. However, fusion at several scales does not by itself specify how tumor evidence is retained and updated to guide fusion at later stages. We propose a progressive multi-scale tumor-state memory network (PMTM) for segmentation from any non-empty subset of T1ce, T1, FLAIR, and T2. PMTM maintains a compact state for the current subject across the encoder stages. At each stage, we use assignment maps to pool spatial features into ordered evidence vectors for each available modality. We average these vectors across the available modalities, and a learned gate combines this evidence with the previous state. The up- dated state guides residual fusion at that stage and is used in the state update at the next stage. A modality-token mixer also models interactions among the available modalities at each stage. We apply semantic supervision to the assignment maps at all four stages. We evaluate PMTM on BraTS2018, BraTS2020, and BraTS2023 GLI across all 15 non-empty modality subsets. Averaged over the three tumor regions and the 15 subsets, PMTM achieves Dice scores of 75.31%, 77.54%, and 80.47% on BraTS2018, BraTS2020, and BraTS2023 GLI, respectively. These scores are higher than those of RobustSeg, RFNet, and mmFormer in our experiments on each dataset. Component ablations and internal state analysis are performed on BraTS2020.

papers.title_en: A General-Purpose Dual-Path Interaction Framework for Multi-View Medical Image Segmentation: Alleviating Data Volume Dependency in Small-Sample Regimes
papers.authors: Shuhuan Wang, Yuanyuan Cui, Pengju Wang, Huimin Guo, Ling Yue, Yin Gu, Yanchao Zhang, Wei Feng, Yunhe Liu, Wei Qian, Mingjun Xu, Shuang Liu, He Ma
papers.evidence: 跨视角解剖融合用于医学图像分割
papers.tldr: 医学图像分割依赖大量标注，小样本下性能明显下降，现有多视图方法常需严格配对样本。作者提出即插即用双路径交互框架DPIF：用Sinkhorn最优传输对齐跨视图分布，以条件互信息引导特征解耦，并用持续同调拓扑正则抑制过拟合。在24个基线、私有超声心动图及两个公开数据集上，多数变体仅用40%–60%数据即接近全量单视图模型性能。该框架为数据稀缺的多视图分割提供了通用可扩展方案。
papers.abstract_en: The performance of medical image segmentation depends on a large amount of annotated data, and most segmentation models experience a significant drop in performance in low-sample-size scenarios. Existing semi-supervised and weakly supervised methods rely on specific network architectures, while traditional multi-view-assisted segmentation methods require strictly paired samples, which limits their clinical applications. To address these issues, we propose DPIF, a general-purpose plug-and-play dual-path interaction framework compatible with arbitrary encoder-decoder segmentation networks, which leverages cross-view anatomical complementarity to reduce annotation reliance. DPIF first performs Sinkhorn optimal transport-based cross-view distribution alignment to establish global semantic correspondence without sample-level pairing. It then adopts conditional mutual information-guided feature decoupling to enable bidirectional knowledge transfer only within the shared semantic space, suppressing view-specific noise. Finally, persistent homology-based topological regularization encodes anatomical invariants as unsupervised priors to mitigate overfitting. Experiments were conducted using 24 baseline models on a private multicenter echocardiography dataset and two public datasets. The results show that DPIF-enhanced models outperform single-view baseline models when trained on comparable amounts of data. Notably, most dual-path variants trained on 40\% - 60\% of the data achieve performance comparable to that of single-view models trained on the full dataset. This demonstrates that DPIF provides a general-purpose and scalable solution for data-scarce multi-view medical image segmentation problems.

papers.title_en: Deep Auxiliary Learning via Bilevel Feature Optimization for Label-Efficient Medical Image Segmentation
papers.authors: Fuping Wu, Xi Jia, Le Zhang, Jiahua Li, Rima Mustafa, Thomas E. Nichols, Bartlomiej W. Papiez
papers.evidence: 基于辅助学习的标签高效医学图像分割
papers.tldr: 医学图像分割的辅助学习通常依赖额外人工标注的辅助标签，导致标注成本显著增加，尤其专家标注昂贵的医学影像场景。为此，本文研究能否利用由现有分割标注自动导出的辅助任务来提升分割性能，并提出一种基于双层优化的辅助学习框架。该方法通过特征通信模块促进主任务与辅助任务间的知识迁移，在三个有限标注医学分割基准上持续优于现有最先进方法。结果表明无需额外人工标注即可获得更优标签效率，为低成本医学图像分割提供了有效方案。
papers.abstract_en: Auxiliary learning (AL), which can improve the performance of a primary task by leveraging related auxiliary tasks, is commonly regarded as a special case of multi-task learning. Existing AL approaches typically require manually annotated auxiliary labels, increasing annotation costs, particularly in medical imaging where expert labeling is expensive. In this work, we investigate whether segmentation performance can be improved using auxiliary tasks whose labels are automatically derived from existing segmentation annotations, requiring no additional manual labeling. To address this, we propose a novel auxiliary learning framework, formulated as a bilevel optimization problem. Our method enables effective knowledge transfer between tasks via a feature communication module, enhancing the primary segmentation task. We evaluate the method on three medical image segmentation benchmarks under limited-label settings. The results demonstrate consistent improvements over state-of-the-art methods, achieving superior label efficiency. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/FupingWu90/ALBO.

papers.title_en: DART: Scaling a Shape Representation Across Anatomical Classes and Imaging Modalities
papers.authors: Koushik Swarna, Pedro R. A. S. Bassi, Lam Ngo, Wenxuan Li, Jiancheng Yang, Alan Yuille, Zongwei Zhou
papers.evidence: 跨类别跨模态共享解剖形状先验以修正分割结果
papers.tldr: 分割模型在难分割结构上仍会产生断裂血管、碎片化腺体等不合理形状，而现有形状表征多局限于固定解剖类别。DART从分割概率中学习共享形状表征，借助解剖文本描述校正概率，无需输入医学图像。它在13个公开基准上取得最高31%的Dice提升，并将单一表征从50类扩展到377类，还能跨模态迁移并修正未训练病灶类别。该工作表明共享形状信息可减少扩展分割覆盖所需的新体素级标注。
papers.abstract_en: Current state-of-the-art segmentation models still produce anatomically implausible shapes, such as broken vessels and fragmented glands, on the structures that are hardest to segment. Learned shape representations capture what structures look like and can help correct these errors, but most cover a fixed set of anatomical classes. Extending this coverage across classes and imaging modalities is costly because it often requires new voxel-level annotations. We propose Diffusion for Anatomical Reshaping with Text (DART), which learns a shared shape representation from segmentation probabilities. It uses anatomical descriptions to correct these probabilities without receiving medical images. Across 13 public benchmarks, absolute Dice gains reach 31% for individual gallbladder cases in CT and 10% for individual prostate cases in MRI. Using existing segmentation predictions, we scale a single shape representation from 50 to 377 anatomical classes without new voxel-level annotations for correction training. The shared representation also corrects four lesion classes absent from training and transfers from CT to MRI without retraining. Corrected labels also improve segmentation models, raising one model's Dice from 57.1% to 67.5%. The same pipeline supports annotations for 45,000 CT scans. These results suggest that sharing shape information within and across classes can reduce the need for new voxel-level annotations when extending segmentation to more anatomical classes and imaging modalities. The model is available at https://huggingface.co/Koushik45/DART-Seg

papers.title_en: Reliability-Guided Vision-Language Decoding with Text-Aware Skip Refinement for Medical Image Segmentation
papers.authors: Sivan Talaei, Fatemeh Daneshfar, Abdulhady Abas Abdullah, Mourad Oussalah
papers.evidence: 面向CT等医学图像的视觉语言引导分割
papers.tldr: 医学图像分割常受目标视觉区分度低、结构不规则及跨模态差异大困扰，文本可缓解歧义但无差别融合会引入不可靠引导。RELiF以可靠性引导解码整合文本，RFG自适应控制跨模态更新，TSRA用文本细化高分辨率特征。在X线、CT和内镜任务上表现有竞争力，并分析效率与稳定性。其可靠性响应还能表征预测不确定性，误差像素处不确定性更高。
papers.abstract_en: Medical image segmentation remains challenging when targets exhibit limited visual distinction, irregular structure, or substantial variation across imaging modalities. Medical text can reduce this ambiguity, but indiscriminate fusion may introduce unreliable guidance. We present RELiF, a vision--language framework that integrates text through reliability-guided decoding. Its Reliability-guided Fusion Gate (RFG) adaptively controls cross-modal updates, while the Text-guided Skip Refinement Adapter (TSRA) refines high-resolution features using text guidance. RELiF is evaluated on radiographic, CT, and endoscopic segmentation tasks, where it shows competitive performance across diverse imaging characteristics and target appearances. Additional analyses examine efficiency and stability. The complementary uncertainty representation derived from the reliability response also shows an association with prediction difficulty, with higher uncertainty values occurring more frequently in pixels associated with segmentation errors. Code: https://github.com/SeivanTalaie/RELiF.

papers.title_en: CAPS: Clinically-Verifiable Anatomy-Prioritized Synthesis for Missing MRI Imputation in Brain Tumor Segmentation
papers.authors: Cecilia Diana-Albelda, Arthur Longuefosse, Mario Rubén Paz Campos, Álvaro García-Martín, Jesus Bescos
papers.evidence: 缺失模态MRI合成与分割联合用于脑肿瘤
papers.tldr: 多参数MRI是脑肿瘤诊疗金标准，但临床常缺失模态，现有分割器黑箱不可解释、合成图像模糊难验证。CAPS提出解剖优先的可验证合成框架，用L1、L_AFP与L_DualDice混合目标约束深层解剖特征和拓扑边界。在BraTS成人胶质瘤上平均Dice达82.38%，并在脑膜瘤、儿童及非洲队列零样本泛化。盲法放射评估显示图像质量与临床效用提升，为缺失模态MRI补全提供可信视觉证据。
papers.abstract_en: Multi-parametric MRI is the gold standard for neuro-oncology, yet acquiring complete 4-modality protocols may be unfeasible in real-world clinical practice. When handling missing modalities, existing automated systems force a critical compromise: robust segmenters operate as uninterpretable "black boxes" that bypass image generation, while standard synthesis models often produce blurry reconstructions lacking diagnostic reliability. To address this issue, we propose CAPS, a Clinically-Verifiable Anatomy-Prioritized Synthesis framework that reconciles computational precision with clinical transparency. Our multi-modal generative architecture is driven by a hybrid objective function (L_1 + L_AFP + L_DualDice) that explicitly enforces the preservation of deep anatomical features and strict topological boundaries, rather than relying solely on pixel-wise optimization. Evaluated comprehensively on the BraTS Adult Glioma dataset, the framework achieves superior synthesis fidelity across intensity-based metrics, and demonstrates robust downstream segmentation performance (82.38% mean Dice), successfully restoring verifiable visual context. Furthermore, the framework exhibits exceptional zero-shot cross-domain generalization, maintaining high structural fidelity across completely unseen Meningioma, Pediatric, and Sub-Saharan African cohorts without domain-specific adaptation. Finally, a blinded radiological assessment confirms that our anatomy-aware approach significantly enhances both perceived image quality and clinical utility, providing clinicians with the reliable visual evidence required to trust downstream automated workflows.

papers.title_en: ReSeg: Retraining-free segmentation of abdominal organs via generalizable semantic representation learning
papers.evidence: 零样本腹部器官分割，可迁移至危及器官勾画
papers.tldr: 腹部器官分割依赖大规模真实数据，泛化与隐私受限。ReSeg采用两阶段免重训练框架：先以合成数据预训练GSRNet学习通用语义表征，再初始化OESNet并生成保持器官空间布局的多样化图像训练分割网络。在CT、MRI、PET三类模态七个数据集上，ReSeg无需真实训练图像即持续优于现有SOTA。该工作为域无关零样本腹部器官分割提供了可泛化新范式。
papers.abstract_en: Abdominal organ segmentation is essential in modern medical applications. While existing deep learning approaches demonstrate promising performance, their heavy reliance on large-scale image data raises concerns over generalization capability and privacy risks. This motivates the development of generalizable segmentation training paradigms based on domain-randomized image synthesis, facilitating generalization across unseen real image domains. However, existing paradigms either suffer from limited segmentation performance when applied to abdominal organs, or require dataset-specific finetuning. To address these limitations, we propose ReSeg, a novel two-stage retraining-free framework for domain-agnostic zero-shot abdominal organ segmentation. At the first stage, our organ-agnostic synthetic data-driven pretraining approach exploits semantically and visually diverse synthetic images generated by a dedicated data engine to optimize a Generalizable Semantic Representation Network (GSRNet). The network is thereby capable of learning semantic features robust against variations in anatomical structure, imaging contrast, resolution and spatial context, which provide universal representation capabilities that serve as a foundation for segmentation learning. Subsequently, in the second stage, we continue to train an Organ-specific Encoder-decoder Segmentation Network (OESNet), whose encoder is initialized with the pretrained weights. This training process is facilitated by another dedicated data engine, which generates diversified visual images while strictly retaining the inherent spatial layout of abdominal organs. Comprehensive evaluation on seven abdominal organ segmentation datasets across three different modalities including CT, MRI, and PET demonstrates that ReSeg consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods while eliminating the need for real training images.

papers.title_en: CVP-BAA: Efficiently Adapting Segment Anything Model for Medical Image Segmentation
papers.authors: Mei Wang, Minghui Li, Libin Lan
papers.evidence: 基于SAM的高效适配用于医学图像分割
papers.tldr: 医学图像分割依赖大量标注和专用架构，SAM的PEFT适配又缺乏局部结构先验、对细粒度细节不敏感。CVP-BAA将卷积特征作为结构先验注入选定ViT块的自注意力键值投影，并并行设计边界感知适配器增强高频边界特征。在三种成像模态五个基准上，其定量指标与定性结果均优于任务专用模型和现有PEFT式SAM适配。该工作以混合PEFT提升SAM对医学纹理与局部细节的敏感性，改善边界勾画。
papers.abstract_en: Various task-specific medical segmentation models have demonstrated strong performance, their heavy reliance on extensive annotations and highly specialized architectures limits their versatility, scalability, and clinical applicability. Recently, adapting vision foundation models, particularly the segment anything model (SAM), has emerged as a promising alternative. However, prevalent parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) strategies, such as prompt tuning and adapter tuning, often lack an explicit mechanism to embed local structural priors into the long-range dependency modeling of vision transformers (ViT), rendering them insufficiently sensitive to fine-grained details. To address these limitations, we introduce CVP-BAA, a novel hybrid PEFT method that improves SAM's sensitivity to domain-specific textures and local details, leading to superior boundary delineation. The proposed CVP-BAA adopts two key ideas. First, it introduces a convolutional visual prompting (CVP) strategy that leverages convolutional features as structural priors, prepending them to the key and value projections within the multi-head self-attention layers of strategically selected ViT blocks. Through a dedicated prompt generation-and-injection module, this mechanism effectively bridges local spatial details with global context semantics. Second, a boundary-aware adapter (BAA) is designed as a parallel branch to the feed-forward network within the same selected blocks. By explicitly computing and amplifying high-frequency components, the BAA enhances feature representations along tissue boundaries and fine-grained lesion structures. Extensive experiments on five benchmarks across three imaging modalities demonstrate that CVP-BAA achieves superior segmentation performance, surpassing existing task-specific models and PEFT-based SAM adaptations in both quantitative metrics and qualitative results.

papers.title_en: nnInteractive Agent: General-Purpose AI Agents as 3D Image Annotators
papers.authors: Fabian Isensee, Constantin Ulrich Harsy, Maximilian Rokuss, Benjamin Hamm, Philipp Vollmuth, Klaus H. Maier-Hein
papers.evidence: 语言驱动的智能体借助交互式分割模型自动完成三维结构标注
papers.tldr: 交互式3D分割模型仍需人工定位目标、放置提示并检查修正。作者将nnInteractive封装为MCP工具，并加入专家提示技能，让通用AI智能体用自然语言完成定位、分割、检查与反馈修正。在14幅CT/MRI/PET/显微CT、51个目标上，Claude Code与Codex仅凭请求达到0.81/0.84平均Dice，告知目标位置后均达0.85。该开源方案把通用智能体变成无需训练的3D图像标注器，并在VoxTell失败场景中保持稳健。
papers.abstract_en: Interactive 3D segmentation models such as nnInteractive turn a few spatial prompts (points, scribbles, boxes) into accurate volumetric masks, but a human still does the annotation work: finding each structure, placing prompts, checking the result and correcting it. General-purpose AI agents can now interpret images, call tools and write code. We show that such agents can take over this work without additional training: the user makes a request in plain language, and the agent works out what has to be segmented, locates the targets, prompts nnInteractive, inspects the 3D result, corrects it and responds to feedback. Asked for 'the muscles used for chewing', an agent identifies and segments the masseters and pterygoids; asked to count liver lesions, it writes its own code to find candidates and splits a merged lesion on request. Our open-source nninteractive-agent provides nnInteractive as tools over the Model Context Protocol (MCP), together with a skill that encodes how experienced users prompt it. On a benchmark spanning CT, MRI, PET and micro-CT of humans, a mouse and an ant (14 images; 51 targets from organs and tumours to muscles, foot bones, vessel trees and an insect brain), Claude Code and Codex reach a mean Dice of 0.81 and 0.84 from the request alone; when told where each target is, both reach 0.85 and prompt nearly as effectively as an oracle that places prompts using the reference segmentation. A text-prompted 3D model (VoxTell) is more accurate on most standard radiological targets but less robust: it returns an empty mask for one of them and fails on the leg muscles, the foot bones, the mouse and the ant, where the agents remain accurate. Code: https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/nninteractive-agent

papers.title_en: Hyperparameter-Free Boundary-Interior t-vMF Dice Loss for Medical Image Segmentation
papers.evidence: 面向医学图像分割的免超参数边界感知Dice损失
papers.tldr: 医学图像分割中，类别不平衡和边界附近误差仍是难题，而自适应 t-vMF Dice Loss 需调超参数。本文提出 STB-tvMF Dice，按边界与内部区域分别自适应确定形状参数，无需调参。在 Synapse 上，U-Net 的平均 DSC 达 70.75%，显著高于自适应版本的 63.03%。该无超参数、边界感知的损失函数为分割训练提供了更稳定有效的方案。
papers.abstract_en: Class imbalance and errors near anatomical boundaries remain challenges in medical image segmentation, motivating loss functions that account for these difficulties. Adaptive t-vMF Dice Loss adjusts the similarity function during training but requires hyperparameter tuning. We propose Self-Tuned Boundary-Aware t-vMF Dice Loss (STB-tvMF Dice), which adapts the function separately for boundary and interior regions without tuning shape-adaptation parameters. Each region's shape parameter of t-vMF function is determined from its mean prediction-target cosine similarity in the preceding epoch and remains fixed throughout the current epoch. This rule maximizes the slope of the similarity function at the observed mean similarity, providing a principled basis for adaptation without validation-based parameter selection. Experiments on three datasets and architectures demonstrated its effectiveness. On Synapse with U-Net, STB-tvMF Dice achieved a mean DSC of 70.75%, compared with 63.03% for Adaptive t-vMF Dice Loss. Our code will be available soon.

papers.title_en: Sam-Correction: Fully Adaptive Label Noise Reduction for Medical Image Segmentation
papers.evidence: 基于SAM的自适应噪声掩膜纠正用于医学分割
papers.tldr: 医学图像分割常受标注噪声影响，而现有校正方法依赖额外高质量GT，获取成本高且不总可行。为此，SAM-Correction利用基础模型以全自适应方式校正噪声GT，并通过与分割网络联合训练生成提示，逐步降低标签噪声。在多种真实标注噪声实验中，该方法能精确降噪并训练出高性能分割模型。其意义在于无需干净标签也可实现鲁棒模型训练。
papers.abstract_en: The quality of the teacher label has a dramatic impact on the outcome of the machine learning process. Medical image segmentation often suffers from a noisy ground truth (GT) mask due to difficulties in consistent annotation. Although a recent study has proposed a promising method to curate the noisy GT mask, this requires additional well-curated GT masks that are not always accessible without the aid of multiple medical experts. As an alternative, we propose SAM-Correction, which utilizes a foundation model to correct the noisy GT mask in a fully adaptive manner instead of manually preparing well-curated masks. In our approach, we progressively mitigate label noise via the segment anything model (SAM), where prompts are given from another segmentation network that we train concurrently. Experiments with various types of label noise derived from actual human annotations demonstrate that SAM-C achieves precise noise reduction and high-performing segmentation models trained thereby. Our method paves the way for robust model training even when clean labels are entirely unavailable.
